transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-10-15 16:00 UTC | Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Morgan Hayes, Ethan Park, Priya Nair (Redwood); Ava Lopez, Jonah Kim, Ralph Ortega, Marta Ruiz (Sentinel Insights)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough): Quick hosted API walkthrough focused on embeddings + rerank endpoints. Discussed integration options (hosted vs dedicated), security questions (SOC2, SSO), pilot plan and next steps for a small A/B evaluation using sentinel's query logs.

00:00:01 Morgan Hayes: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm morgan from redwood inference. quick check — can you all hear me ok?
00:00:06 Ava Lopez: yes loud and clear, thanks morgan.
00:00:08 Morgan Hayes: great. quick round robin, ethan park is our search se, priya's on cs and will help on onboarding. who do we have from sentinel?
00:00:16 Jonah Kim: hey this is jonah, i'm on search infra.
00:00:18 Ralph Ortega: ralph here, cto. short on time today but wanted to attend for context.
00:00:22 Marta Ruiz: marta, vp data.
00:00:24 Morgan Hayes: awesome. agenda — one, run through hosted embeddings + rerank api flow; two, show console and optimize suggestions for batching/quant profiles; three, discuss security/compliance and pilot next steps. sound ok?
00:00:36 Ava Lopez: yup sounds good.

00:01:10 Ethan Park: all right jumping in — i'll start with a quick diagram of the hosted flow. so you call our embeddings endpoint, get back embeddings, then pass top-k candidates through rerank which calls a thin scoring endpoint that combines model relevance with signals. typically we do a two-stage retrieval: cheap vector similarity then model-based rerank.
00:01:28 Jonah Kim: is that rerank happening server-side inside redwood or do we host the model and call it from our infra?
00:01:33 Ethan Park: good q — for hosted api mode the model and inference runtime live in redwood's runtime. you send an api call with doc ids or the candidate payload, and the reranker executes as part of the request. so network overhead is just the api call and payload. if you need on-prem we also have private deployments but that's a separate track.
00:01:52 Jonah Kim: ok got it, so no extra infra for us in hosted.

00:02:30 Morgan Hayes: i want to surface cost/latency tradeoffs up front. reranking costs scale with candidate count and sequence length; so if you push 1000 candidates it's more expensive. typical pattern is 50-200 candidates then model rerank top 10. that balances quality/cost.
00:02:45 Ava Lopez: we've been doing 200 candidates today with algolia's hybrid step, curious what latency we'd see.
00:02:51 Ethan Park: latency measures depend on model and quantization. in hosted we have small-llm variants optimized for rerank that give 50-150ms p95 for a 100-candidate rerank in many cases. important note — our reported numbers assume request batching and prefix caching; if you send one-off requests you'll see higher p95.
00:03:12 Jonah Kim: when you say prefix caching — is that the kv cash? sorry, kv cash?
00:03:18 Ethan Park: (laughs) yes bad transcript — i meant KV cache. it's our ability to cache shared keys for repeated prefixes which helps chat-like flows and some rerank warm paths.

00:04:01 Morgan Hayes: demo time — i'm going to share my screen. pulling up the console. so here is the embeddings playground, you can upload a small dataset or paste text and generate embeddings. once you have vectors you can run a nearest-neighbor call using our search api then pipe candidates into the rerank endpoint.
00:04:23 Ava Lopez: can you show a real example with our sample product docs?
00:04:28 Morgan Hayes: i have a seeded demo doc set — i'll run a sample query 'how to configure alerting thresholds' and show top-5 unranked results then apply rerank.
00:04:37 [00:04:37] Morgan Hayes: running embeddings /search call...
00:04:50 [00:04:50] Morgan Hayes: here are the top raw vector matches — note you can specify vector index type, and we support approximate nearest neighbor backends.
00:05:05 [00:05:05] Ethan Park: and here's the rerank request. payload looks like {query:..., candidates:[{id:..., text:...}, ...], context:...}. you'll get back a sorted list with scores and explanation tokens if you enable interpretability flags.
00:05:24 Jonah Kim: that explanation token thing — how heavy is that on latency?
00:05:29 Ethan Park: marginally heavier, we run a small attribution pass. it's optional and we usually recommend enabling it during tuning, then turning it off in prod once weights are locked.

00:06:10 Ava Lopez: quick security q — does hosted mode store our documents? we can't have customer data persisted in logs.
00:06:18 Priya Nair: good question — hosted mode by default stores minimal telemetry for billing. content persistence is opt-in; we offer a no-retention policy for enterprise. we also have KMS integrations and SOC 2 Type II already.
00:06:33 Marta Ruiz: do you support our SSO (SAML Okta) and RBAC for team-level separation?
00:06:38 Morgan Hayes: yes — SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning, role-based access in the console, and audit logs that you can forward to your SIEM. i'll drop the links in the follow up.

00:07:15 Ralph Ortega: curious about model versioning — we need deterministic results for A/B over time. how do you pin versions?
00:07:22 Ethan Park: you can pin model revisions in the API call (model: "redwood-rerank-v1@2026-09-21") and in the console there's a rollout mechanism for canary then full. we also store artifacts and can snapshot key metrics per model version for reproducibility.

00:08:05 Morgan Hayes: switching to Optimize — this is where we show batching/caching suggestions. you can upload request logs and Optimize will recommend batch size, quant profile, and candidate pruning thresholds. in this tenant we recommend a 16-32 batch for throughput-y workloads.
00:08:25 Jonah Kim: are those suggestions actionable via the api or do we have to re-deploy?
00:08:28 Morgan Hayes: actionable — Optimize writes a config that you can apply to your route. no full redeploy needed for many params, it's runtime-configurable.

00:09:12 Ava Lopez: pricing — can you give a rough estimate for a pilot? we expect ~2M queries/month, 200 candidates average, and a 3-5k doc set for initial test.
00:09:25 Morgan Hayes: rough back-of-envelope — embeddings cost per vector and rerank cost per candidate-token. for a pilot i'd prepare a small committed cap, but to be concrete i'll send a pricing deck with sample math.
00:09:40 Marta Ruiz: ok please include unit economics examples. we need to compare to our current algolia spend.

00:10:05 Ethan Park: quick technical deep-dive note — if you have long documents we support chunked embeddings and document-level metadata. for rerank we preserve doc-level context and can pass summarized context to reduce sequence length.
00:10:22 Jonah Kim: about latency SLOs — do you have an SLA for hosted endpoints?
00:10:27 Morgan Hayes: hosted has P99 and P95 targets for paid tiers; dedicated reserved capacity comes with an SLA. we'll include the SLA matrix in follow up.

00:11:00 Ava Lopez: any constraints on dataset types? we have binary attachments, markdown, huge configs.
00:11:06 Ethan Park: attachments get converted to text during ingestion inside the console; for protected docs you can ingest in your private deployment. metadata retention is configurable.

00:12:00 Morgan Hayes: quick demo of console trace — here's a trace for a rerank request showing time spent in vector retrieval, rerank model, and network. the top contributor in this demo was model exec, so we showed a suggestion: drop candidate set to 75 and use a quant profile q4-native for that model to cut cost by ~35% with <1% quality drop.
00:12:30 Marta Ruiz: tell me more about quant profile risk — are there hallucination regression risks?
00:12:36 Ethan Park: there is slight risk; Optimize runs regression evals on a prompt set you provide. it'll show you quality deltas. for safety-critical responses, we recommend a higher-fidelity profile or canary traffic split.

00:13:40 Jonah Kim: network topology — how's data routed? do you have regional endpoints in eu-west?
00:13:46 Morgan Hayes: yes regional endpoints and routing policies. you can pin traffic to region and we support fallback regions. for eu-west data residency we have dedicated region hosting.

00:15:10 Ava Lopez: next up — pilot plan. we want a low-friction pilot: you host embeddings + rerank, we send logs and evaluate relative ndcg on our queries. what's a normal timeline?
00:15:20 Morgan Hayes: typical pilot 2-4 weeks: week 1 ingest sample docs + integration, week 2 run A/B with 5-10k queries, week 3 tune batch/cand thresholds and run benchmarks, week 4 decision. we'll help with benchmarking harness.
00:15:37 Ava Lopez: ok that aligns. can you run a quick live A/B with our sample query set?
00:15:42 Ethan Park: we asked for the sample last week but didn't get it yet — if you can drop the subset to the shared drive i'll seed it into the trial now.
00:15:50 Ava Lopez: i'll upload right after this call.

00:16:30 Morgan Hayes: quick Q from ralph — how do you handle PII? we need redaction and encryption at rest.
00:16:36 Priya Nair: we support field-level redaction on ingestion and you can opt for customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). at-rest encryption is standard. we can also sign a data processing agreement for the pilot.
00:17:05 Ralph Ortega: good. also procurement note — our security team will want SOC/ISO docs and possibly a pentest summary.
00:17:11 Morgan Hayes: yes we'll include SOC2 and ISO artifacts and our pentest summary in the follow up.

00:18:00 Ethan Park: demo follow — showing an API call example for rerank with candidates compressed via ids only — this saves network and serialization time. we also support streaming partial rerank results if you're doing progressive UI.
00:18:22 Jonah Kim: streaming rerank sounds interesting — any sdk support?
00:18:26 Ethan Park: node/python SDKs both support streaming responses. we'll share code snippets.

00:19:10 Ava Lopez: objection — if we go hosted and traffic spikes, can you autoscale? we can't afford big latency spikes during Black Friday like events.
00:19:20 Morgan Hayes: hosted has autoscaling and burst capacity tiers. for high-variance workloads we recommend a Dedicated pool or reserved capacity to guarantee throughput. we can propose a hybrid: hosted for most traffic, dedicated reserved for seasonal peaks.
00:19:40 Marta Ruiz: any contractual minimums?
00:19:43 Morgan Hayes: pilot's no min; dedicated has commit contracts. we'll outline in the pricing doc.

00:20:30 Ethan Park: i'll show a quick benchmark run — p95 about 140ms for this dataset with 100 candidates, rerank v1, q4-native. if you take q2-int8 you'd see lower memory / cost but slightly higher p95.
00:20:48 Jonah Kim: what's model reproducibility for audits? we need to be able to show how a result was produced.
00:20:52 Ethan Park: we persist model revision ids and can export request traces with inputs, candidate ids, model scores, and the reranker logits for a TTL you configure. for long-term retention we can integrate with your archive storage.

00:22:15 Morgan Hayes: we're about halfway through time — any outstanding questions?
00:22:21 Ava Lopez: can you also confirm the data path for embeddings? we don't want raw content leaving our VPC in some cases.
00:22:29 Morgan Hayes: noted — for sensitive datasets we recommend private deployment or VPC peering. hosted with no-retention helps but if you need zero egress we can discuss private.

00:23:50 Marta Ruiz: one more on legal — do you sign our standard dpa?
00:23:55 Morgan Hayes: we'll have legal look at your DPA; many customers use our standard addendum but we can negotiate.

00:25:10 Morgan Hayes: quick recap and proposal: we'll provision a 30-day trial tenant, you upload 50k-document subset and ~5-10k sample queries, ethan will prepare the benchmark harness and a tuned rerank config, we'll run A/B and share ndcg metrics. security artifacts and pricing deck to follow.
00:25:34 Ava Lopez: perfect. thanks.

00:26:00 Morgan Hayes: any other final asks?
00:26:03 Jonah Kim: can you include a sample script for candidate pruning?
00:26:07 Ethan Park: yes i'll add that to the benchmark pack.

00:27:10 Morgan Hayes: ok i'm going to close the demo, i'll attach console screenshots, api snippets, and the Optimize suggestions in the follow-up email.
00:27:20 Priya Nair: i'll create the pilot workspace and invite your team — expect invites in 24 hours.
00:27:28 Ava Lopez: we'll upload the sample dataset after this call. thanks all.

00:27:45 Morgan Hayes: thanks everyone, speak soon.

Action items recap (auto-generated): Morgan to send pricing + docs; Ethan to prep benchmark; Ava to upload dataset; Marta to confirm compliance contact.
